title: Mullin Completes the Double as Baker's Lead Turns to Dust
title_candidates: Mullin Completes the Double as Baker's Lead Turns to Dust
Eagle at Eight, Ruin by Sixteen
Worst Round in TEG History Settles the Spoon
theme: A tale of two collapses at Bletchingley: one handed David Mullin a rare double, the other decided who finished last.
opening_hook: Jon Baker stood on the 8th tee with an eagle in hand and a seven-shot lead in the Trophy; by the time he reached the 16th he had neither, and David Mullin had both the Trophy and the Green Jacket he came for.

round_story.subject: David Mullin's unremarkable final round is nonetheless the best round of the day, and the one that wins the tournament.
round_story.why_it_matters: On a day when everyone around him fell apart, Mullin's round produced the field's best net score (1) and best gross score (19) — nothing spectacular on paper, but it was exactly enough, delivered at exactly the right time.
round_story.shape: Setup: Mullin starts the day level with Jon Baker for the Trophy lead. Turn: while Baker charges clear with an eagle, Mullin simply compiles pars through the 4th to 6th and shrugs off a quadruple bogey at the 7th. Resolution: with the best net and gross scores of the day banked, Mullin takes outright control of the Trophy at the 12th and never lets go.
headline_candidates: The Quietest Best Round of the Day
round_story.chosen_headline: The Quietest Best Round of the Day
round_story.standfirst: No eagles, no fireworks — just the best net and gross scores in the field, delivered on the day it mattered most.

race_story.subject: David Mullin completes the Trophy-Jacket double as Jon Baker's seven-shot lead disintegrates and Gregg Williams inherits the Wooden Spoon.
race_story.why_it_matters: This is the final round: the Trophy, the Green Jacket and the Wooden Spoon are all settled here, and David Mullin's double is only the second in TEG history, following TEG 2.
race_story.shape: Setup: Baker draws level then eagles the 8th to lead the Trophy by seven, while Henry Meller clings to the bottom of the Spoon table by four. Turn: Baker's back nine collapses completely as Mullin's card holds firm, and simultaneously Gregg Williams's ruinous +43 gross round overtakes Meller for last place. Resolution: Mullin wins the Trophy by eight and the Jacket by nineteen — his second career double — while the Wooden Spoon changes hands on the final day, Williams beating Meller to it by five.
headline_candidates: Mullin Completes the Double at Last
Double Glory as Spoon Changes Hands
race_story.chosen_headline: Mullin Completes the Double at Last
race_story.standfirst: A seven-shot lead disappeared, the bottom of the table changed hands, and only one man finished the week where he started it: on top.

discovered_storylines.subject: Jon Baker eagles the 8th to lead the Trophy by seven, then loses it by the close.
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: This single round is the mechanism by which the Trophy was lost rather than won — a front nine good enough to win the whole tournament outright, followed by a back nine that gave it all back and more.
discovered_storylines.shape: Setup: level with Mullin overnight, Baker eagles the par-4 8th to move seven clear. Turn: from the 9th he goes seven holes without a net par, including a sextuple bogey at the short 12th and an even worse sextuple bogey at the par-5 15th, bleeding 27 gross shots across eight holes. Resolution: a brilliant front nine is buried under a ruinous back nine, and the Trophy — and with it the Jacket — passes to David Mullin.
headline_candidates: Eagle at Eight, Ruin by Sixteen
discovered_storylines.chosen_headline: Eagle at Eight, Ruin by Sixteen
discovered_storylines.standfirst: An eagle that should have won him the Trophy instead marked the high point of a round that lost it.

discovered_storylines.subject: Gregg Williams's Wooden Spoon-clinching round is the worst gross round recorded in TEG history to date.
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: Henry Meller's two quintuple bogeys looked like they would keep him anchored at the bottom of the table, but Williams's own collapse — his personal worst on both counts, and the worst gross round anyone has posted in 55 TEG rounds — proved worse still.
discovered_storylines.shape: Setup: Meller starts the day four adrift at the bottom of the Spoon table, needing only to stay out of trouble. Turn: he obliges with quintuple bogeys at the 11th and 15th, dropping to the foot of the table — but Williams's own card is unravelling faster, a 43-gross disaster including 16 shots bled over the closing six holes. Resolution: Williams's collapse overtakes Meller by five strokes and hands him his first Wooden Spoon.
headline_candidates: Williams's Round Sets a New Low
Spoon Swaps Hands at the Death
discovered_storylines.standfirst: Forty-three over gross was enough to leapfrog Henry Meller into last place on the final day.

race_state_note: Mullin's Trophy win is classed as 'inherited' — Baker's collapse handed it to him rather than any surge of his own — while the Jacket was built steadily across all four rounds, with Mullin never finishing worse than second.
